newsitem.title: UK: London gold steadier at fix after Friday's fall.
newsitem.headline: London gold steadier at fix after Friday's fall.

text.p: There was little sign of a follow-through to New York's late Friday rally when the week opened quietly for precious metals in Europe, dealers said.
"After all the moves last week, it would not be surprising if they took a breather this week," one dealer said.
Platinum, having given the upward impetus to the complex, was showing signs of a correction on Monday having come off a $407-bid high on Friday but gold was steady.
Bullion fixed at $361.80 per ounce after $358.60 on Friday when the correction from recent highs was in full swing and driven by New York.
"Gold has held steady while platinum and palladium have come off. Technically its top looks to be around $365," a dealer said.
However he added that gold may have seen the high in its current phase and if it corrected, a return to $358.00 was technically feasible.

Hong Kong overreached in trying to push the price higher earlier following up on New York's close which saw bullion end at $363.00/$363.50 pulled up by late buying on Comex which took the April contract to a $365.10 close, up $4.10.
"Honk Kong was just a bit too bullish," a dealer said.
Platinum was indicated at $390.50/$391.50 at 1045 GMT, up a dollar having opened one down.
The correction in platinum on Friday was much more dramatic than in the other metals and reflected the precariousness of its rise from around $371.00 last Monday to Friday's high.
"The push (to $407) in Tokyo on Friday might be the last blow-out of that phase. It could take a breather now," a dealer said.
Technical analysts warned that since platinum challenged its highs from May last year on Friday, a period of much more volatile prices was likely.
There was little price impact from a decision to strike by workers at Russia's nickel-platinum-palladium mining and refining combine Norilsk at the weekend over unpaid wages in 10-days time.
"It was pretty much in the price already," a dealer said.
But there were no reported moves to bring Russian and Japanese negotiators to the table to begin talks on platinum and palladium export contracts for 1997.
Palladium was indicated barely changed at $150.50/$151.50 and silver was up seven cents with gold at $5.30/$5.32.
